full_judgment: 24. Another test as to taking cognizance in a case under either section 4 of the Act, 1958 or under sections 190 or 193 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is that the order passed by a court for taking cognizance with any languages, statements and decisions from which it can be inferred that he opted to apply his discretion to take cognizance. From the statements/words used in the present case it can be inferred from the above impugned order, in particular, the specific terms used by the learned Judge he opted to exercise his discretion to take cognizance. In this regard we hold that the laws regarding cognizance mentioned above the Judge, Magistrate or Court of Sessions has given discretion to take cognizance or not. We also hold that it can be inferred from the language used or word placed in the impugned dated 14-9-2014 order are sufficient as it is not the assumption or presumption but a logical inference can be drawn from the present impugned order and it is sufficient under the relevant provisions of law. The inference from the impugned order also includes that the court has considered the documents and records and after applying his judicial mind the learned court has taken cognizance as has been sufficient for taking cognizance as per the provisions of law thus no illegality has been committed by the learned Special Judge in passing the impugned order dated 14-9-2014. Accordingly, we are not inclined to interfere with the impugned order passed on 14-9-2014 for taking cognizance in his case.
